newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to streamline natgas project approvals.
newsitem.headline: Australia to streamline natgas project approvals.

text.p: The Australian government on Monday unveiled what it called the final phase of its natural gas industry reform programme.

Resources and Energy Minister Warwick Parer told a gas industry forum he would set up a special project facilitation section within his department to cut red tape and streamline approval procedures to avoid the delay of valuable gas projects.

He pointed to the announcement last week that Woodside Petroleum Ltd and the Royal Dutch/Shell Group would consider building a A$10 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant near Darwin in northern Australia.

"I am determined to ensure that government red tape does not delay this valuable project, which would double Australia's LNG exports and add one percentage point to gross domestic product," Parer said.
"The project facilitation division will be able to assist Woodside and Shell with their feasibility study, and will ensure that there are no government impediments," he said.

Prime Minister John Howard's major projects facilitator, Bob Mansfield, and the project facilitation division would also focus on the proposed Comalco Ltd alumina refinery near Gladstone, the proposed Korea Zinc Co Ltd plant at Townsville, and Chevron Corp's Papua New Guinea to Queensland pipeline, he said.
As part of the reforms, Parer named Leigh Clifford, CRA Ltd managing director, to head a gas reform implementation group.
"Mr Clifford will provide a strategic leadership and oversight in the crucial final decision-making phase of the gas reform process," Parer said.
The group would help agreement on policy by making it easier for the public, industry and users talk to each other, he said.
Parer said the government would release an energy policy paper, or white paper, later this year but did not say when.
"This paper will ensure the policy settings are such that Australia is well placed to meet economic and environmental opportunities and challenges at home and overseas over the next 25 years."
